scope.files: Every repository-owned .hx file in the checkout is scanned, including compiler, target API, fixtures, examples, templates, and future runtime tooling.
scope.policy: Untyped values never enter semantic compiler logic. An unavoidable external or negative-test boundary is exact-source allowlisted, validates immediately into the named closed model, and has malformed-input evidence.

constructs.description: Haxe Any erases the static value contract.
Haxe Dynamic defers member and conversion checks.
haxe.Json.parse returns an untyped external value.
DynamicAccess is an open-ended string-keyed value carrier.
Private-access metadata bypasses the declared visibility contract.
Raw __c__ calls bypass typed IR and structural C AST lowering.
Reflect member access replaces a known structural type with runtime lookup.
The Haxe cast keyword can assert a type without validating the value shape.
The Haxe untyped keyword disables ordinary type checking.

allowlist.justification: The reviewed Reflaxe ownership file is external JSON and the pinned Haxe parser necessarily returns an untyped value.
allowlist.validation: The adapter immediately checks schema version, activity scalar types, the generated-file array, every string entry, path normalization, duplicates, and ownership-manifest exclusion before returning the closed record.

allowlist.justification: The negative aggregate fixture must present the real Haxe Dynamic semantic type to prove it cannot masquerade as a structurally known value record.
allowlist.validation: CBodyLowering rejects the signature before constructing HxcIR and the aggregate suite requires exact source-positioned HXC1001 with no generated artifact.

allowlist.typedModel: Float expression and validated HxcIR arithmetic operations
allowlist.justification: The fixture needs a real cast node to check that cast-wrapped division stays outside the direct integer-division proof. The operand already has type Float; the cast introduces no foreign value.
allowlist.validation: The arithmetic suite requires the general floating division operation in HxcIR. Its strict native harness independently checks that input 47 returns 5.

allowlist.justification: The negative test must forge an impossible enum-abstract value to prove the typed diagnostic registry rejects unallocated IDs.
allowlist.validation: The forged value is used only for the rejecting call and the fixture fails unless CDiagnostic.definition throws.

allowlist.typedModel: HxcIRDynamicPlan, HxcIRDynamicOperation, and generated hxrt_value adapters
allowlist.justification: The differential fixture must use the real Haxe Dynamic type so Eval and generated C exercise the same boxes, casts, member operations, calls, equality, null, and type-value behavior.
allowlist.validation: One private alias contains the untyped spelling; the Dynamic differential compares Eval with strict native C, checks forced-collection ownership, verifies closed numeric adapters, and rejects unsupported shapes without output.

allowlist.typedModel: CBodyValueType and validated HxcIR primitive operations
allowlist.justification: The fixture needs a real Dynamic operand to prove that runtime-typed division cannot enter the signed-Int optimization. Replacing it with Int would remove the rejecting case.
allowlist.validation: The Dynamic differential requires source-positioned HXC1001 with the exact unsupported division marker. It also requires that no generated output remains.

allowlist.typedModel: closed generated Dynamic adapters without capturing closures
allowlist.justification: The fixture needs a real Dynamic receiver before it can prove that extracting one of its methods does not silently create an unsupported capturing closure.
allowlist.validation: The Dynamic differential requires exact HXC1001 rejection at the bound-method boundary and verifies that no generated artifact remains.

allowlist.typedModel: closed generated Dynamic adapters without capturing closures
allowlist.justification: The negative fixture must request the natural Haxe bound-method value so the compiler proves it will not lower that value as a bare function pointer with lost receiver identity.
allowlist.validation: The Dynamic differential requires exact HXC1001 rejection at the bound-method boundary and verifies that no generated artifact remains.

allowlist.justification: The fixture needs a real Dynamic record before it can prove that a runtime member name does not bypass the compiler's closed numeric member-token plan.
allowlist.validation: The Dynamic differential requires exact HXC1001 rejection for the computed lookup and verifies that no generated artifact remains.

allowlist.justification: The negative fixture must call the real reflection API with a runtime String to prove that computed member names remain outside the admitted closed-world Dynamic slice.
allowlist.validation: The Dynamic differential requires exact HXC1001 rejection for the computed lookup and verifies that no generated artifact remains.

allowlist.typedModel: HxcIR managed-root publication for local Dynamic values
allowlist.justification: The negative fixture must declare a real Dynamic global to prove the current local-value ownership contract does not silently publish an unplanned global root.
allowlist.validation: The Dynamic differential requires exact HXC1001 rejection for the global carrier and verifies that no generated artifact remains.

allowlist.typedModel: exact Dynamic equality plans for admitted source types
allowlist.justification: The fixture needs a real Dynamic payload-enum operand to prove the compiler does not substitute tag-only equality for recursive typed payload semantics.
allowlist.validation: The Dynamic differential requires exact HXC1001 rejection before payload-enum boxing and verifies that no generated artifact remains.

allowlist.typedModel: exact Dynamic equality plans for admitted source types
allowlist.justification: The second real Dynamic operand keeps the requested payload-enum equality shape explicit instead of testing a weaker mixed typed comparison.
allowlist.validation: The Dynamic differential requires exact HXC1001 rejection before payload-enum boxing and verifies that no generated artifact remains.

allowlist.typedModel: closed Dynamic plans with exact source-type identity
allowlist.justification: The negative fixture must box a real interface-typed value to prove that unresolved polymorphic identity never becomes an implicit universal Dynamic adapter.
allowlist.validation: The Dynamic differential requires exact HXC1001 rejection for unresolved polymorphic identity and verifies that no generated artifact remains.

allowlist.justification: The scalar fixture must use the real Dynamic type to prove an Int box, cast, and equality need the carrier runtime but no managed allocation or collector.
allowlist.validation: The Dynamic differential inspects the exact runtime plan and generated source, then compiles strict native C while rejecting allocation, object, and collector features.

allowlist.justification: The scalar fixture must use the real Dynamic type to prove a Float box and cast need the carrier runtime but no managed allocation or collector.
allowlist.validation: The Dynamic differential inspects the exact runtime plan and generated source, then compiles strict native C while rejecting allocation, object, and collector features.

allowlist.justification: The scalar fixture must use the real Dynamic type to prove a Bool box and cast need the carrier runtime but no managed allocation or collector.
allowlist.validation: The Dynamic differential inspects the exact runtime plan and generated source, then compiles strict native C while rejecting allocation, object, and collector features.

allowlist.justification: The scalar fixture must use the real Dynamic type to prove null boxing and equality need the carrier runtime but no managed allocation or collector.
allowlist.validation: The Dynamic differential inspects the exact runtime plan and generated source, then compiles strict native C while rejecting allocation, object, and collector features.

allowlist.justification: The negative fixture must present the real Haxe Dynamic key type to prove ObjectMap does not choose structural equality, pointer accidents, or an implicit universal box.
allowlist.validation: CBodyTypedMap rejects the key before HxcIR and artifact emission, and the object-enum-map differential requires the exact source-positioned HXC1001 diagnostic with no generated output.

allowlist.typedModel: HxcIRType.IRTDynamic and the contained exception carrier
allowlist.justification: The fixture must use the real Haxe exception payload type so throw and catch exercise source-language Dynamic transport instead of a compiler-owned substitute.
allowlist.validation: One private alias contains the untyped spelling. The exception suite verifies exact primitive and managed payload identity across generated calls, cleanup, strict C11, and native sanitizers.

allowlist.typedModel: Int payload in the contained exception carrier
allowlist.justification: The fixture must perform the real Haxe Dynamic-to-Int exception narrowing that the admitted lowering implements.
allowlist.validation: The value is created from the function's typed Int input, crosses one generated call and rethrow, and must return unchanged in strict native execution.

allowlist.typedModel: Counter identity in the contained exception carrier
allowlist.justification: The fixture must narrow the real Dynamic exception payload back to its collector-owned Counter identity after unwinding a generated callee.
allowlist.validation: The same function creates the Counter immediately before the throw, and strict native execution plus sanitizers verify its identity, field value, root lifetime, and cleanup.

allowlist.typedModel: Int payload in the contained exception carrier
allowlist.justification: The cleanup fixture must recover the real Haxe Dynamic-to-Int payload after a managed String owner unwinds.
allowlist.validation: The typed Int input is thrown directly, and strict native execution plus sanitizers require the same value after String cleanup without leaks or stale roots.

allowlist.justification: The negative specialization fixture must pass the real Haxe Dynamic semantic type to a generic call so it can prove that Dynamic never becomes a closed specialization key or an implicit boxed fallback.
allowlist.validation: CGenericTypeCanonicalizer rejects the argument before graph lowering, and the generic-specialization suite requires exact source-positioned HXC1001 at the call with no generated artifact, including across a warm compiler-server request.

allowlist.justification: The reference-interpreter fixture must exercise the real Haxe Dynamic type so the independent oracle measures source-language casts, calls, equality, null, and evaluation order rather than a compiler-owned imitation.
allowlist.validation: One private alias contains the only untyped spelling; values remain inside the standalone reference fixture, while the HxcIR suite models the corresponding compiler contract with closed Dynamic plan and operation records.

allowlist.justification: This fixture intentionally represents the real Haxe Dynamic language type so HxcIR can prove it is modeled explicitly rather than used as an internal escape hatch.
allowlist.validation: The HxcIR suite exercises the explicit IRTDynamic variant and validator rejection paths; the value is not part of compiler implementation state.

allowlist.justification: The negative interface fixture must present the real Haxe parent-to-child cast so haxe.c can prove that a fat interface value is never reinterpreted without the future runtime type proof.
allowlist.validation: CBodyLowering rejects the cast at its exact source position with unsafe-interface-downcast-needs-runtime-type-proof, and the virtual-dispatch suite requires HXC1001 with no generated artifact.

allowlist.justification: The negative interface fixture must present a real Haxe cast between unrelated interfaces so matching C carrier shapes cannot erase their nominal source-language identities.
allowlist.validation: CBodyLowering rejects the cast at its exact source position with unrelated-interface-conversion, and the virtual-dispatch suite requires HXC1001 with no generated artifact.
